text: Continuous Integration (CI) is a software development practice where developers frequently merge their code changes into a shared repository. Each merge triggers an automated build, which compiles the code and packages it for deployment. Following the build, a series of automated tests run to check for bugs, broken features, or compatibility problems. The main goal of CI is to catch issues early, before they become complex and expensive to fix. This is managed through CI pipelines—sequences of steps that handle building, testing, and sometimes deploying the code. When a pipeline fails, the team is notified immediately, allowing them to address the problem right away. Ultimately, CI helps teams work more efficiently, reduce errors, and deliver higher-quality software faster.
